ideas.title: Climb anything
ideas.critique: Holding only while the force stays inside the Coulomb cone, with friction set by the material, is the first version where the grip comes from physics and not a budget, and the slip on the wet gutter is earned rather than staged. The risk is the same as before and bigger now: IPC contact on an affine body sitting on a thin gutter lip is where jitter and creep start, and a film where Lumi trembles on the ledge or teleports over the lip reads as one more glitch reel like the stomp takes.

ideas.title: The bees and the smoker
ideas.critique: Fewer, bigger, meshed bees with real flight, plus a 230 Hz wingbeat that the shutter blurs, tackles the failure of the firefly take, where the specks pulsed and barely moved. Smoke with buoyancy and wind plus a scent field makes this a real herding toy. The weak point is the film at bee height: a few hundred bees in a thin grey haze can still read as dots in fog, and 'chase warm bodies' tends to collapse into everyone orbiting the nearest friend.

ideas.title: A rope bridge you tie yourself
ideas.critique: A structure whose quality you feel underfoot is a strong loop, and a catenary sag with a wave running along it at each step is motion the island has never had. The rope already exists on the island (Tied together), the building UI for tying and knotting planks is the likely sink of the session, and 'a heavy friend tips everyone into the water' is a gag that tends to end up as a triggered event.

ideas.title: The island floods at spring tide
ideas.critique: Saint-Venant with wetting and drying over the real terrain is honest engineering, and water finding the actual gaps is something to read. But 'the sea comes over the low shore' is the payoff the seesaw and the levelling game already delivered, and flooding the island falls under the wrecking cap. The sods and the tub are the only new play, and the event comes once a month, so a player rarely meets it.
